'''Günter Schmahl''' (26 March 1936 – 14 August 2018)<ref name="faz:todesanz" /><ref name="www-xrm2018:mem" /> was a German physicist, professor at the [[University of Göttingen]] and a pioneer of [[X-ray microscopy]].

The main focus of Schmahl's work, and his most important achievement, was the development of full-field [[Soft x-ray microscopy|soft X-ray microscopy]]. He was one of the first to recognize the potential of this method and to identify and follow the technological approach of using [[zone plate]]s as lenses in such a microscope.<ref name="www-roentgenmuseum1992" /><ref group="P" name="schmahl1969" /><ref group="P" name="niemann1974" /> Schmahl and his collaborators further developed the technique until it was ready for application in two- and three-dimensional imaging of biological samples.<ref name="www-welt1995" /><ref group="P" name="schmahl1988depatent" /><ref group="P" name="schmahl1989uspatent" /><ref group="P" name="schmahl1995" /><ref group="P" name="weiss2000" />

Schmahl founded the Institute for X-ray Physics at the University of Göttingen and headed it until his retirement in 2002.<ref name="www-irp" /> He was also one of the founders and the first organizer of the [[International Conference on X-Ray Microscopy]], which has been held every three years since 1983 and biennially since 2008.<ref name="www-xrm2018:hist" />

== Honors and awards ==

* 1985: [[Lower Saxony State Prize]], category Science<ref name="www-ndspreis" />
* 1992: Röntgen Medal of the city of [[Remscheid]]<ref name="www-roentgenmuseum1992" />
* 1995: Röntgen Award of the Department of Physics and Crystallography at the [[University of Würzburg]]<ref name="physbl1995vol51no12" />
* Since 1996: Member of the [[Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]<ref name="www-adwgoe" />
* 2005: [[Advanced Photon Source]] Compton Award, [[Argonne National Laboratory]], Argonne, Illinois (together with [[Janos Kirz]])<ref name="www-compton" />
